Hi Chuck,

I'm sorry. You've now chased us twice. Nobody has come back to you since Hal pinned the fault on October 25, and my reply on November 1 didn't lead to anything either. That's not good enough, especially after all the careful testing you did for us.

I checked your order this morning. The replacement power supply hasn't been sent yet, so there's no tracking for me to give you. I've put your request back in front of the team as overdue. It's for one Mean Well LRS-50-5, the 5V supply, going to the address on your order, and nothing needs to come back from you. A colleague is picking it up today and will reply in this thread.

Until then, keep running the two good units and leave the faulty supply unplugged.

Sarah

**Notes for the team:**
- **No replacement has been sent.** Shop···· has no replacement order in Shopify and nothing in ShipBob beyond the original August delivery. We don't stock the LRS-50-5 as a product, so I couldn't create one myself.
- **Flagged as "other":** "Ship one replacement LRS-50-5 to (address hidden)." This is his second chase. The November 1 flag got no action.
- **Not an RMA.** The note on this ticket says Hal found no hardware fault and there's no RMA, but that's outdated. The October 25 swap test showed the fault follows one supply. I haven't promised him a date or tracking.

Hi Sarah,

The second PS on my BitaxeC2 just showed a fault in my swarm page. Thats
two PS's that arent working properly now. I have attached a picture to show
the swarm page. Plus NO one has gotten back to me since my last email to
you three days ago.

If you remember or read back through previous emails, you will see that the
PS on the BitaxeC2 was originally on the BitaxeT but you had me swap them
to see if the problem followed the PS.

The BitaxeBCH ps is still chugging along but it drops down to as low as
4.6v but mainly stays at 4.7V but both say "Danger: Low Voltage". I know
you said to not worry about the voltage after I bumped it up to 5.1 but
something isn't right.

Thanks,
Chuck

Hi Chuck,

You're right, and I'm sorry. My last reply only said I'd passed it on, and then nobody got back to you. That's three weeks now since you proved the fault follows the supply. You've done everything we asked, carefully, and you deserved an answer a long time ago.

I've read both screenshots. BitaxeC2 is showing a Power Fault at 5.0 W with 3 minutes of uptime. BitaxeBCH is hashing fine at 1.80 TH/s, but its input reads 4.7V with the Danger: Low Voltage warning. You're also right that something isn't right. The supply now on BitaxeC2 is the one that started out on BitaxeT. That makes two supplies that have faulted. A third sagging to 4.6V with the screw already at 5.1V is lower than I'd expect from cable loss alone. I'm no longer treating this as one bad supply. It looks like the supplies themselves.

For now, unplug the supply on BitaxeC2 from the wall and leave that Bitaxe off, like BitaxeT. BitaxeBCH can keep running. If you want to take some load off its supply, go to Settings in AxeOS and lower the frequency one step from 875 MHz. It will draw less current, which should ease the voltage sag. If BitaxeBCH throws a fault too, switch it off.

I've put this back to the team as a request to replace the supplies. It now covers both faulty ones, and I've asked them to look at the third. Our hardware lead can also check whether there's a wider problem with these supplies. The team is offline right now and picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET. Their answer will come to you in this thread. In the meantime, if you'd like to talk the voltage readings through with our hardware lead, you can post in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate.

Sarah

**Notes for the team:**
- **What I flagged:** a fresh "other" flag asking for 2, likely 3, replacement LRS-50-5 supplies for Shop····, going to (address hidden). It also asks JD to check whether a batch of these supplies is bad before choosing what to send.
- **Still nothing sent:** this is Chuck's third chase, and the November 1 and November 9 flags got no action. No replacement order or return exists, and we don't sell the LRS-50-5, so I couldn't create one myself.
- **The note on this ticket is wrong:** it still says Hal found no hardware fault. The swap test and this second fault both point to the supplies. I haven't promised Chuck how many supplies he'll get, or when.
See if this works. If not, I'll do like last time and send one at a time.

Hi Chuck,

Both came through fine this time, so there's no need to send them one at a time.

They're the same two screenshots I went through in my last email, and they're now with the request to replace the supplies. On the Swarm page, BitaxeC2 shows the Power Fault at 5.0 W. The BitaxeBCH dashboard shows 4.7V with the Danger: Low Voltage warning. My last email still stands. Keep the supply on BitaxeC2 unplugged. BitaxeBCH can keep running, and you can lower its frequency a step if you'd like to take some load off its supply.

One small thing I spotted: BitaxeC2 is on AxeOS v2.14.2 and BitaxeBCH is on v2.15.4. It won't fix the faulty supply, but it's worth updating C2 from its Update page once it's back on a good supply.

The team picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and their answer will come to you here.

Sarah

**Note for the team:** I didn't raise a new flag. Chuck only resent the same two screenshots, and the flag I raised a few minutes earlier already covers them.
Thanks :)

Hi Chuck,

**Possible send problem:** the thread shows my last two replies to Chuck as a one-line "I've passed this to the team…" instead of what I actually wrote. If those emails went out that way, he never got the advice from tonight: unplug the supply on BitaxeC2 and update its firmware. It's worth checking what reached him.
